class.name: TickNetwork
class.brief_description: Tick based network: an authority with client prediction and interpolation, or an owner for each object.
class.description: Synchronizes the [TickObject] nodes over a [TickTransport], in fixed ticks. With [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE] (the default), one peer is the authority, called the server in this reference: peer 1 in a star ([EnetStarTransport]), or [member authority_peer] in a mesh ([EnetMeshTransport], [EnetHostedMeshTransport]). It simulates every object, moving each one with the input of its controller. The other peers are its clients: a client predicts the objects it controls and rewinds them when the server disagrees; the other objects are interpolated [member interpolation_delay] seconds behind the server, or simulated as dolls in a mesh (see [member TickObject.remote_mode]). With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED], for meshes of trusted servers, every object has an owner node that simulates it; the other nodes interpolate it, and nobody predicts. Ownership moves through [member registry_peer], and the nodes follow the timeline of [member clock_master]. A process can run several networks, for example a mesh with other servers and a star with its own clients that follows the mesh's timeline (see [member clock_network]). The network ticks during the physics process; set [member ticks_per_second] equal to [member ProjectSettings.physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second], so bodies moved with the physics delta (like [method CharacterBody3D.move_and_slide]) advance one tick at a time. The client uses the server's tick rate. The client's clock is synchronized with the server's, and the client runs ahead of the server just enough for its inputs to arrive in time, adapting its speed to the network conditions.

method.name: get_event_frame
method.description: Returns the frame [param seconds] after the current one. To run an event at the same frame on every peer, the server sends it for a frame far enough ahead to cover the latency, for example [code]get_event_frame(0.5)[/code].

method.name: get_frame
method.description: Returns the next frame to simulate. Clients run ahead of the server.

method.name: get_local_peer_id
method.description: Returns the id of this peer in the transport, or 0 when not running.

method.name: get_rtt
method.description: Returns the round trip time to the node this peer takes its clock from, in seconds, as measured by the clock synchronization: the server for a client, or [member clock_master] with [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]. 0 on that node itself.

method.name: get_state_at
method.description: Returns the state of [param object] (a [TickObject]) at [param frame] of the authority's timeline, as a [Dictionary] of the declared properties, interpolated when [param frame] has a fraction. Empty when the frame isn't in the history (see [member history_size]). On the server, every simulated frame; on a client, the snapshots it received, its own predicted frames and its dolls' frames. Use it to validate an action in the past (lag compensation): the client sends [method get_view_frame] with the action, and the server checks it against the state it had at that frame. Only with [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE].

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns a [Dictionary] with statistics: [code]rewinds[/code], [code]rewound_frames[/code], [code]ghost_inputs[/code] (inputs repeated by the server because they were missing), [code]late_inputs[/code], [code]rejected_inputs[/code], [code]full_snapshots_sent[/code], [code]delta_snapshots_sent[/code], [code]snapshots_received[/code], [code]snapshots_dropped[/code], [code]malformed_packets[/code], [code]rate_limited_packets[/code], [code]events_sent[/code], [code]events_received[/code], [code]events_rejected[/code], [code]spawns[/code], [code]despawns[/code], [code]time_scale[/code] (the client's speed adjustment), [code]timeline_frame[/code] (this peer's estimate of the authority's current frame, negative while unknown), [code]latest_snapshot_frame[/code], and for dolls (see [member TickObject.remote_mode]): [code]doll_rewinds[/code], [code]doll_rewound_frames[/code], [code]doll_corrections[/code], [code]doll_resyncs[/code], [code]doll_ghost_inputs[/code], [code]doll_suspensions[/code] (dolls left to the snapshots for two seconds because their controller's inputs disagreed with the authority more than this peer pays to simulate again), [code]doll_delays[/code] (a [Dictionary] with how many frames the dolls of each peer are behind this peer's timeline), [code]split_snapshots[/code] (server: deltas sent in more than one datagram), [code]incomplete_snapshots[/code] (client: split deltas dropped because a part was lost) and [code]relevance_changes[/code] (see [member interest_filter]). With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: [code]states_sent[/code], [code]states_received[/code], [code]stale_states[/code] (states of a former owner or of an old version), [code]late_states[/code] (states dropped by their frame: a newer one had arrived, or the frame is far ahead of this node's; many in a row mean the nodes' timelines are apart), [code]malformed_packets[/code], [code]unexpected_packets[/code] (well formed, but for a role or a state this node doesn't have: a few are expected whenever the roles move), [code]transfers[/code], [code]orphans[/code], [code]denied_requests[/code], [code]events_sent[/code], [code]events_received[/code], [code]events_forwarded[/code], [code]events_rejected[/code], [code]spawns[/code], [code]despawns[/code], [code]role_changes[/code], [code]roles_term[/code] (how many times the roles moved in the mesh), [code]has_quorum[/code] (see [method has_role_quorum]) and [code]timeline_frame[/code].

method.name: get_transport
method.description: Returns the transport passed to [method start].

method.name: get_view_frame
method.description: Returns the frame of the authority's timeline shown now by the interpolated objects, with a fraction: on a client, behind the authority by [member interpolation_delay]; on the server, its current frame. Negative while unknown.

method.name: has_role_quorum
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this node is connected to [member role_quorum] nodes of the mesh, itself included, or if there's no quorum to check. A node that has the registry or the clock and loses its quorum is probably the one cut off from the mesh: the game should stop what it does on behalf of every node until this is [code]true[/code] again, or until [signal roles_changed] tells it the roles moved.

method.name: is_object_relevant
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the state of [param object] is sent to [param peer]. On a client, [param peer] is ignored: it tells whether this client gets it.

method.name: is_predicting
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] on a client once its clock is synchronized and it predicts its objects.

method.name: is_rewinding
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while a client simulates again past frames after a correction. Use it to skip side effects (sounds, particles) during the rewind.

method.name: is_server
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this peer is the server (see [member authority_peer]). Always [code]false[/code] with [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: see [method TickObject.is_owner].

method.name: send_event
method.description: Sends an event without target object, received with [signal event_received]. From a client, it goes to the server, for [param frame] (by default, the frame the client predicts). From the server, it goes to [param peer], or every client with 0, and runs on arrival or, with [param frame], when the client's simulation reaches that frame. The name of the event takes at most 255 bytes in UTF-8; the [param payload] can't contain objects nor reals that aren't finite (NaN or an infinity: no value sent through the network has them, also inside arrays and dictionaries), and is limited to [member max_event_size] bytes. Events aren't repeated during rewinds.

method.name: set_object_relevant
method.description: Server: starts or stops sending [param object] to [param peer] (0: every client). An object is always relevant to its controller. With an [member interest_filter], the filter's next answer overrides this. Only with [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE].

method.name: set_roles
method.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: sets [member registry_peer] and [member clock_master] together. While the network runs, both move to connected nodes with one change ([signal roles_changed] is emitted once on every node); returns [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE] if one of them isn't connected. Before [method start], it sets the configured values.

method.name: start
method.description: Starts the network over [param transport]. With [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE], the peer [member authority_peer] (1 by default) is the server; the others are clients and join when connected to it. With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED], every node joins the other nodes of the mesh as they connect.

method.name: stop
method.description: Stops the network. The objects stay registered and synchronize again on the next [method start]. It can be called from the network's own callbacks and signals (an event, [method TickObject._process_tick]): the network then finishes what it was doing first, and [method start] works again once that call returns.

members.member: [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE]: one peer ([member authority_peer]) simulates every object — the server of a star, or one node of a mesh. [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: every object has an owner node that simulates it and sends its state to the other nodes, and ownership can change (see [method TickObject.request_authority]); for trusted meshes of servers, without prediction.

With [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE]: the peer that simulates every object, is the destination of inputs and events, and is the clock master — the hub of a star (1), or the node of a mesh chosen by the project. It changes with a host migration (see [signal host_migrated]).

With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: the node whose timeline the others follow. Every node must start with the same one. While the network runs, setting it moves the clock for the whole mesh (to a connected node; [method set_roles] moves both roles at once), and reading it gives the current one; the configured value stays for the next [method start]. When its node leaves, a successor takes the clock (see [member registry_peer]). After a change, the other nodes go on from the timeline they followed while they measure the new clock, then move to it gradually: the simulation doesn't pause, and the frames neither jump nor go back. A clock master that restarted takes the mesh's current frame from the other nodes. See [signal roles_changed].

Another [TickNetwork] of this process whose timeline this one follows (only for the [member authority_peer] of this network). A game server's star with its clients follows the cluster's network, so the clients, the game server and the cluster's authority use the same frames. Place the followed network before this one in the tree.

Whether every object is relevant to every client until told otherwise ([method set_object_relevant], [member interest_filter]). With [code]false[/code], a client only gets the objects it controls until others are made relevant.

Called on the server as [code]validator(sender: int, event: StringName, payload: Variant) -> bool[/code] for each event without target object sent by a client; returning [code]false[/code] refuses it. Without a validator, those events are accepted.
Frames of history kept for snapshots, predictions and interpolation.
Number of past inputs repeated in each input packet, against packet loss.

Server: a [Callable] that receives a peer id and a [TickObject] and returns [code]true[/code] if the object is relevant to that peer, [code]false[/code] if not, or anything else for no change. Called for every client and object every [member interest_interval] ticks, and when an object is registered with a client. Relevance is decided by the game (distance, rooms, teams); the network only stops sending what isn't relevant.
Ticks between calls to the [member interest_filter].

If [code]false[/code], the objects this peer doesn't simulate get the state of the latest snapshot without interpolation. Use it on game servers that relay a cluster's objects to their own clients, so only the final clients interpolate.
How far behind the server, in seconds, the interpolated objects are rendered.
With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: owners send the state of every object at least every [member keyframe_interval] ticks, even if it didn't change; in between, only the objects that changed.
Largest event payload, in bytes. With [constant TRUST_UNTRUSTED], larger events from clients are refused.
With [constant TRUST_UNTRUSTED], the events each client can send per second (with a burst of the same size); the excess is dropped.
Largest number of inputs the client tries to keep buffered on the server.
Smallest number of inputs the client tries to keep buffered on the server; more jitter increases it up to [member max_input_buffer].

With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: the node that keeps the registry of owners. Every change of owner goes through it and increases the object's version; state with an older version is discarded. Every node must start with the same one. While the network runs, setting it moves the registry for the whole mesh (to a connected node; [method set_roles] moves both roles at once), and reading it gives the current one; the configured value stays for the next [method start]. When its node leaves, a successor takes the registry (and the clock, if the node had both): the first of [member role_candidates] in the mesh or, without candidates, the node with the lowest id. It takes over once no node it's connected to still reaches the node that left, so a node that only lost its own link to the registry doesn't take its place, and only with its [member role_quorum]. It first merges every node's view of the objects, so they keep their ids and owners; the objects of the node that left become orphans, and its spawns become the registry's (see [TickSpawner]). Requests waiting for the previous registry are denied ([signal authority_request_denied]). While nobody can take the registry, no ownership changes ([method TickObject.request_authority] and the like return [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE]) and the objects go on with their owners. The registry's own objects are the reference for the variables an object declares: a node whose object declares others doesn't synchronize it, and prints an error. A node that comes back finds its roles on another node and joins as a plain node. If nobody took them and it restarted, it takes them again like a successor, from what the other nodes know, instead of starting them over. See [signal roles_changed].

With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: the nodes that take the registry and the clock when their node leaves, by order of preference: usually the node that starts with them, then its reserves. Empty (the default): any node, the lowest id first. Every node must have the same list (a node with another one is refused), set before [method start]. With candidates, the roles of a node that left stay with nobody while no candidate is in the mesh (see [member registry_peer]). [codeblock] # Node 1 has the registry and the clock, and node 2 is its reserve; the other nodes never take them. $Mesh.role_candidates = PackedInt32Array([1, 2]) [/codeblock]

With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: how many nodes of the mesh, this one included, a node must be connected to in order to take the registry or the clock, or to go on answering as the registry. 0 (the default) doesn't check. With more than half of the mesh (2 of 3, 3 of 5), a mesh that splits never gets a second registry: the smaller part waits. A registry without its quorum keeps what it knows, answers nothing and doesn't orphan the objects of the nodes it lost, until it has its quorum again or finds that the roles moved. Set it before [method start], to the same value on every node. See [method has_role_quorum] and [signal role_quorum_changed].
Node the paths of the objects are relative to. The same object must have the same path on every peer.
The server sends a snapshot every [member snapshot_interval] ticks.
Ticks per second of the simulation, 1000 at most. Clients use the server's value.

How much the server trusts the clients. With [constant TRUST_UNTRUSTED], it limits the rate and size of what they send (inputs, events and pings), drops a client that acknowledges no snapshot for 30 seconds, and accepts an event for an object only from its controller unless [method TickObject._validate_event] decides. On the other peers of a mesh, the frames a doll is simulated again have a budget (see [constant TickObject.REMOTE_MODE_DOLL]). The input of an object is always taken only from its controller, and state only from the server. It only applies to [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE]: with [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED], every node is trusted, and [method start] prints a warning while this is [constant TRUST_UNTRUSTED].

signal.name: authority_changed
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted on every node when the owner of [param object] changes ([param new_owner] is 0 when nobody owns it).

signal.name: authority_orphaned
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted on every node when the owner of [param object] left (or released it to nobody). Nobody simulates it until the project assigns it, for example with [method TickObject.assign_authority]. [param last_frame] is the frame of its last known state.

signal.name: authority_request_denied
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted when what this node asked for [param object] doesn't happen. A request ([method TickObject.request_authority], [method TickObject.assign_authority]) is refused when another transfer of the object was in progress, when its owner refused it, or when the registry moved to another node before answering (see [member registry_peer]). A release ([method TickObject.release_authority]) doesn't happen when the registry can't take it (it has no quorum, see [member role_quorum]), or is lost or moved before answering: the object stays with this node, simulated again.

signal.name: event_received
signal.description: Emitted when an event without target object runs: on the server for events from clients, on clients for events from the server ([param sender] is 1). [param frame] is the frame the event was sent for.

signal.name: host_migrated
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE] over an [EnetHostedMeshTransport]: the host [param old_host] left and [param new_host] is the authority now. The new authority goes on from the latest state it had, with the same objects and timeline; the objects the old host controlled (its NPCs and its own player) are now controlled by the new one, so the game may want to remove the old host's player. The spawns of the old host are the new authority's too (see [TickSpawner]). The others join the new authority again, like after a reconnection. [SceneMultiplayer] doesn't follow: see [signal TickMultiplayerPeer.host_migrated].

signal.name: peer_left
signal.description: Emitted when a client leaves (on the server) or when the connection with the server is lost (on a client). With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted when a node of the mesh leaves.

signal.name: peer_ready
signal.description: Emitted on the server when a client passes the handshake, and on a client when the server accepts it ([param peer] is the server). With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted when another node of the mesh passes the handshake.

signal.name: prediction_started
signal.description: Emitted on a client when its clock is synchronized and it starts predicting its objects.

signal.name: rejected
signal.description: Emitted on a client when the server refuses it, for example because of a different protocol version (another version of the module) or precision build. With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted when another node of the mesh refuses this one, for the same reasons, or because both started with a different [member registry_peer], [member clock_master] or [member role_candidates].

signal.name: relevance_changed
signal.description: Client: the server started or stopped sending the state of [param object]. A hidden object keeps its last state; hide or remove it as the game needs.

signal.name: rewound
signal.description: Emitted on a client after a rewind: the predicted objects diverged from the server at [param frame], and [param frame_count] frames were simulated again.

signal.name: role_quorum_changed
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED] and a [member role_quorum]: this node got, or lost, the nodes it needs to take or keep the registry and the clock (see [method has_role_quorum]).

signal.name: roles_changed
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: the registry or the clock master moved to another node, because the project changed it or because its node left, or the node that had it restarted and took it again (see [member registry_peer]). Emitted on every node; compare with [method get_local_peer_id] to know whether this node has a role now.

constants.constant: The clients may be modified or malicious: the server limits and validates what they send. The default.
The peers are trusted (for example, servers of the same cluster): no rate or size limits, and events are accepted from any peer.

Every object has an owner node, and ownership can change. Every node is trusted (events, ownership, spawns): use it only between servers you control. [member registry_peer] and [member clock_master] move when their node leaves (see [member role_candidates] and [member role_quorum]), or when the project changes them.
